title: Add evals framework
description: This PR introduces a framework for running agent evals. It adds new Makefile commands for eval workflows, provides a robust pytest configuration for evals (including API key handling and model matrix support), and introduces a variety of realistic datasets for testing and benchmarking data cleaning, enrichment, and analysis scenarios. These changes lay the groundwork for automated and reproducible evaluation of LLM-powered agents on structured data tasks.

title: feat: HTTP REST API
description: This PR introduces support for running the Sweet server as an HTTP REST API, in addition to the existing MCP protocol. It adds new dependencies for HTTP support, updates CLI options to allow selecting the protocol and configuring the server address, and implements the HTTP server startup logic.

title: Remove duplicate recipe MCP tools and CLI command
description:
- Remove old sweet_run_recipe/sweet_list_recipes tool definitions (replaced by enhanced versions with params, stop_on_error, recipe_dir support)
- Consolidate handlers to use workspace.run_recipe/list_recipes
- Remove dead-code handlers that were unreachable due to earlier elif
- Remove old 'sweet list-recipes' CLI command (superseded by 'sweet recipe list')
- Keep sweet_run_steps tool and handler (distinct functionality)

title: Phase 3.2
description: This PR introduces a new "recipe" system for reusable multi-step data workflows, integrating it throughout the CLI, core workspace, and tool interfaces. The most significant changes are the addition of new CLI commands for listing and running recipes, support for recipes in the workspace API, and exposing recipe-related actions as tools for programmatic use.

title: Phase 2.3
description: This PR introduces a new data quality validation feature to the codebase, allowing users to validate datasets against configurable rules via both the CLI and programmatic interfaces. The changes add a `validate` command to the CLI, extend the core workspace with a validation method, and integrate a new tool for data quality checks into the MCP interface.

title: Phase 6.3 6.4
description: This PR introduces advanced anomaly detection and cross-dataset intelligence features. It adds new CLI commands and core APIs for detecting and explaining anomalies, discovering relationships between datasets, and automatically joining tables. These capabilities are also exposed as tools for programmatic and LLM-driven workflows. Comprehensive tests for anomaly detection are included to ensure correctness and robustness.

title: Phase 6.5
description: This PR introduces new natural language (NL) transformation capabilities, allowing users to describe data transformations in plain English and have them automatically translated and applied to datasets. The changes include new CLI commands, workspace methods, and integration with the tool interface, making NL transforms accessible both via the command line and programmatically.

title: Phase 5.4
description: This PR introduces a new "team conventions" system, allowing teams to define, validate, and enforce data conventions (such as naming, type preferences, and data quality) via a `.sweet/conventions.yaml` file. The changes add CLI commands, a conventions data model and validator, workspace integration, and new tools for the MCP agent to interact with conventions.

title: Phase 6.2
description: This PR introduces a data synthesis and augmentation feature set. It adds new CLI commands, core logic for synthetic data generation, imputation, and augmentation, and integrates these capabilities into both the Workspace API and the agent tool interface. These changes enable users to easily generate realistic synthetic datasets, fill missing values with various strategies, and add derived columns for data enrichment.

title: Phase 6.1
description: This PR introduces new semantic data understanding capabilities to the `sweet` CLI and backend, enabling users to infer semantic types for dataset columns and discover potential join relationships across datasets. The changes span the CLI, core workspace logic, and tool integration for programmatic access.

title: Phase 5.3
description: This PR introduces a new feature for creating, sharing, and restoring portable workspace bundles in the `.sweet` format. These bundles encapsulate all sheets, transforms, and operation history, making it easy to save and share complete workspace states. The changes include new CLI commands, core serialization logic, and integration with the MCP tool system.

title: Phase 5.2
description: This PR introduces a new system for learning, surfacing, and managing usage patterns within the CLI and backend. It enables the application to observe user behaviors, suggest actions based on frequent patterns, and provides tools to inspect and manage these learned patterns. The main changes include new CLI commands for pattern management, backend support for learning and suggesting patterns, and new tools for programmatic access to pattern data.

title: Phase 5.1
description: This PR adds a new feature for suggesting data transformation actions based on detected data patterns, both as a CLI command and as a programmatic tool. The main changes introduce a `suggest` command to the CLI, a corresponding `suggest` method in the `Workspace` class, and integration of this feature into the toolset for programmatic use. This enables users and automated agents to receive actionable suggestions for cleaning and transforming datasets.

title: Phase 4.6
description: This PR introduces version control features for tabular data. It adds the ability to create, view, and manage versioned snapshots ("commits") of datasets, compare changes between versions, and restore previous states. These features are exposed via both the CLI and programmatic interfaces, and are thoroughly tested with a new suite of unit tests. Additionally, new tools are registered for use in the agent interface.

title: Phase 4.4
description: This PR introduces notebook integration, enabling rich interactive data inspection within Jupyter and Marimo notebooks. The main addition is the new `SweetWidget` class, which provides HTML-rendered, interactive views of DataFrames, as well as a `%sweet` IPython magic for quick visualization. Extensive tests are included to ensure robust functionality and integration.

title: Phase 4.5
description: This PR introduces a new integration with the Great Tables library, enabling the export of publication-quality HTML tables from Sweet workspaces and Polars DataFrames. The changes add both user-facing CLI functionality and programmatic APIs, along with comprehensive tests. The update also exposes this capability as an MCP tool for broader automation and agent use.

title: Phase 4.2
description: This PR adds a unified export system to the project, enabling data to be exported from the workspace to local files, cloud storage (such as S3 or GCS), and databases (such as PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, DuckDB). It introduces a new `export` CLI command, a core `exporters` module, and expands the `Workspace.export()` method and tool interface to support these destinations and formats.

title: Phase 4.1
description: This PR introduces major enhancements to the data loading capabilities of the `sweet` project, enabling seamless loading from local files, URLs (including cloud storage and web tables), and databases. It also adds comprehensive tests for these new connectors and expands the CLI and tool interface to support these new data sources.

title: Phase 4.3
description: This PR introduces a new feature for generating production-ready pipeline code in multiple formats (Polars, SQL, dbt, and script) from a workspace's data transform history. It adds a new CLI command, API, and tool integration for this functionality, along with comprehensive tests to ensure correctness across formats and edge cases.

title: Phase 3.5 multi agent pipeline
description: This PR introduces specialized data processing agents and a flexible pipeline orchestration system to the `sweet` package. It adds four new agents (`IngestionAgent`, `QualityAgent`, `TransformAgent`, `ExportAgent`) and a `Pipeline` class that allows chaining these agents into multi-stage workflows. The CLI and programmatic interfaces are updated to support running pipelines with customizable stages, and tests are included to validate the new functionality.

title: Phase 3.4 agent memory
description:
This PR introduces a persistent memory system for Sweet agents, enabling them to remember user preferences, domain rules, and run history across sessions. It adds a new `AgentMemory` module, integrates memory features into the agent workflow, and exposes memory management commands via both the CLI and the agent's tool interface.

title: Phase 3 agentic workflows
description: This PR introduces a reusable "recipe" system for orchestrating multi-step data workflows, both as a Python API and via the CLI. It adds YAML-based recipe definitions, a registry for built-in and user recipes, and new CLI/MCP commands for running recipes or arbitrary step sequences. These changes make it easier to define, share, and execute complex data workflows with validation, rollback, and reporting.

title: Phase 2 intelligent data
description: This PR adds several new CLI commands and tool definitions to enhance data profiling, validation, and analysis capabilities, primarily by integrating Pointblank for statistical profiling and validation. It introduces commands for deep column profiling, data validation, type/outlier/PII detection, column cast suggestions, contract inference, and correlation analysis. These features are also exposed as tools for programmatic access in the MCP protocol.

title: Add agent foundation
description: This PR introduces several enhancements, focusing on expanding its CLI with new headless commands, improving modularity, and exposing additional core functionality. The most significant changes are the addition of new CLI subcommands for data transformation, profiling, SQL querying, code generation, and server mode, as well as updates to the package's module exports and dependency management.

title: feat: Add DB/SQL mode
description:
This adds the ability to load/inspect a DB file, providing specialized tools for:

- table selection
- AI assistance via the Sweet AI Assistant (attuned to SQL transformation workflows)
- writing to flat files (CSV, TSV, Parquet)

title: feat: handle loading of large datasets
description:
This PR allows large datasets to be quickly loaded/viewed in the DataGrid. Navigational affordances (e.g., the `:row` command) make it easy to get to specific places in very large datasets.

UI controls such as the row adder are moved to the bottom-most row slice. And dataset dimensions have been added to the info bar.

title: feat: sweet AI assistant in the Tools drawer
description:
This PR adds the Sweet AI Assistant, which allows you to discuss and transform your data interactively. The conversational AI capabilities complement Sweet's data manipulation workflow, integrating LLM-powered assistance directly into the terminal interface (in the Tools drawer). It's built on the `chatlas` library with automatic provider fallback (Anthropic Claude preferred, OpenAI GPT secondary), the assistant intelligently distinguishes between conversational data exploration queries and transformation requests using advanced code detection logic.

When users ask exploratory questions like "describe this data" or "what patterns do you see?", the assistant provides immediate conversational insights without requiring approval. However, when users request actual data transformations like "add a calculated column" or "filter these rows", the assistant generates precise Polars code. We provide a fairly comprehensive API reference covering 200+ operations from Polars 1.32.0+ so that it won't have problems with delivery to the transformation approval workflow.

The system requires only a simple .env file with an API key (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY`) and automatically generates dataset context including column types, sample values, and statistics to provide the LLM with complete understanding of the user's current data. This creates a pretty good chat experience for data exploration while maintaining Sweet's preview-before-execute approach for all data modifications.

title: feat: add Find mode for specific columns in Tools
description: This PR adds column search functionality, placing the controls for this in the Tools drawer. When in Find mode, the interface provides visual feedback and several ways to break out of the mode.

title: feat: include ways to add new values
description:
This PR is all about making it easier to add new values to a table. Here's a short list of improvements:

- explicit display of None values in cells
- better cell editing experience (double click to edit, editable value is entirely selected in modal, better handling of incompatible types)
- column names now display information on type in info bar
- affordances for adding rows and columns now placed at boundaries of table limits
